alerts.title: DTG-associated hyperglycemia: pre-diabetes now present
alerts.message: Guidelines state hyperglycemia has been reported among HIV patients on DTG, and clients with 2+ risk factors for hyperglycemia and high baseline glucose should not be on DTG. This patient has multiple risk factors: age ≥30 (36 years), family history of DM, and BMI ≥25 (32.4 kg/m²). Since starting DTG 18 months ago, fasting glucose rose from 92 to 118 mg/dL and HbA1c is 6.1% (pre-diabetic range). Acanthosis nigricans confirms insulin resistance. Evidence for drug attribution: DTG is known to cause hyperglycemia, and the temporal relationship with DTG initiation supports it. Evidence against: family history of DM and obesity are independent risk factors. Guidelines recommend switching to EFV400 or ATV/r-based regimen for clients with hyperglycemia risk factors and elevated glucose.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess whether DTG should be continued given pre-diabetes and multiple hyperglycemia risk factors. Consider switching to EFV400 or ATV/r-based regimen per guidelines. Refer for diabetes management.

alerts.title: Significant weight gain and obesity on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines note obesity increases risk of heart disease and diabetes. Patient gained 17 kg in 18 months on DTG (65 kg to 82 kg), BMI rising from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m², now classified as obese. Waist circumference 96 cm indicates central adiposity. This degree of rapid weight gain is clinically significant and compounds her hyperglycemia risk. DTG is temporally associated with the weight gain. The patient reports clothes no longer fitting. Guidelines list weight gain as a modifiable risk factor and note that if weight does not allow for use of available DTG formulations, alternative regimens should be considered. No clinician plan addresses this weight gain or its metabolic consequences.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate whether DTG-associated weight gain warrants regimen change. Provide lifestyle counselling. Consider alternative ART regimen if weight gain continues or metabolic complications worsen.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia with elevated LDL and triglycerides
alerts.message: Guidelines note dyslipidemia as a complication in PLHIV and list it alongside rapid weight gain as a risk factor for diabetes development. Patient's lipid profile is abnormal: total cholesterol 228 mg/dL, LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL, triglycerides 212 mg/dL. This atherogenic pattern, combined with obesity (BMI 32.4), elevated BP (138/88), and pre-diabetes, significantly increases cardiovascular risk. DTG-associated weight gain may be contributing to the dyslipidemia. No baseline lipid values are available for comparison. No clinician plan addresses lipid management or cardiovascular risk assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess cardiovascular risk. Consider dietary counselling, lipid-lowering therapy if indicated, and evaluate whether DTG contribution to dyslipidemia warrants regimen modification.

alerts.title: Missing glucose monitoring per DTG guidelines
alerts.message: Guidelines state clients with 2+ hyperglycemia risk factors and normal baseline glucose who are initiated on DTG should have RBS or FBS monitored every 3 months for 6 months. This patient had multiple risk factors (age ≥30, family history of DM, BMI ≥25) at DTG transition 18 months ago with baseline fasting glucose of 92 mg/dL (normal). There is no evidence in the record that quarterly glucose monitoring was performed during the first 6 months or at any interval since. Current fasting glucose of 118 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.1% confirm progression to pre-diabetes that may have been detected earlier with appropriate monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Institute regular glucose monitoring every 3 months. Given current pre-diabetes, follow diabetes screening and management guidelines for ongoing surveillance.
